_note: 2026-10-08, overhang walls as Orca 2.4.2 finds and prints them (a wall more than half the nozzle past the layer below, at the bridge flow) and a face on a cutting plane cut as the top of the part below: the reference X now gets the overhang walls Orca 2.4.2 gives it (overhang wall filament on x-reference 6.6 to 6.3 mm against Orca's 6.3). 2026-10-06, travel acceleration and jerk as Orca's GCode::_extrude writes them: only for a travel that moves (the nozzle not already at the path's first point, or a layer change's lift still owed), so paths joined end to start (a zig-zag solid fill) no longer get a travel jerk and a print jerk line between them; the reference plate loses 14 M204/M205 lines and is otherwise unchanged (filament and time estimate equal). 2026-10-04, the layer fan as Orca's CoolingBuffer and GCodeWriter::set_fan work it out: layers slower than fan_cooling_layer_time stop the fan unless reduce_fan_stop_start_freq keeps it at the minimum (Orca default off, so the reference plate's slow layers write M106 S0 where they wrote the minimum), interpolated speeds are whole percents, and a percent becomes 255.5 per hundred cut to an integer (43 percent is S109, was S111). 2026-10-04, line widths as Orca's _extrude writes them: a ;WIDTH: line only when the width as written (thousandths) changes, carried over from the layer below (and always after the prime tower), so the reference plate drops the repeated ones. 2026-10-03, the filament list of sharded files: every ;@L layer marker also lists the filaments its paths print with, and the `; filament:` line of a Bambu Lab header is a placeholder that finalize fills from all of them, so a file sliced in shards lists the plate's filaments, not only those of the shard that holds the header. Finished files are unchanged (77 benchmark requests compared); the reference plate's unfinalized text gains the list on each layer marker. 2026-10-03, progress as Orca's G-code processor writes it: a ;@P line at the top of the start marks where finalize puts the first M73 P0 R, and finalize writes M73 P R after every move whose share or minutes change instead of only at layer changes; Bambu Lab files get Orca's header, configuration and executable blocks. The reference plate's G-code gains the ;@P line (its unfinalized text). 2026-10-03, cooling as Orca's CoolingBuffer on the written layer: a layer short enough for the slowdown or the fan to respond is written once and timed the cooling buffer's way (moves at their feed rates from the first extrusion, travels, the retractions the writer really makes, wipes and custom G-code inside the layer such as a bed slinger's timelapse shot), and its slowdown is worked out again with that time; the fan reads it too. Before, the paths' model left out the timelapse block and counted a retraction for every travel over the minimum, so short layers came out slower than Orca's. 2026-10-02, the aegis fast path also takes islands whose outline has bumps shallower than half the smallest printable feature (a rough mesh surface): what the opening loses there lies within that depth of the outline, the skeleton follows such bumps the same way, and on the bench models every wall it writes stays within 0.05 mm of the skeleton's with the same line counts and widths (filament within 0.06 percent). 2026-10-02, aegis walls of an island that is thick everywhere are the outline moved in by each bead's distance (round at concave corners), written without building the skeleton: the same lines, bead widths and direction as the skeleton's, every wall within 0.05 mm of it. 2026-10-02, the first and the last layer use top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap (Orca default 25 percent) for their infill area; the layer change retracts where Orca's change_layer does: after before_layer_change_gcode and the progress line, before layer_change_gcode and the fan. 2026-10-01, a layer prints island by island as Orca's process_layer does (each island's walls, then its infill), walls and slices are simplified at the profile's resolution (Orca's m_scaled_resolution) instead of a fixed 0.0125 mm, and a travel to support that stays inside one support island does not retract (Orca needs_retraction); support paths chain nearest first, a tree island keeping its own order. Before that, Orca parity paths: brim and skirt print at the first layer infill speed (support speed above it), brim loops are ordered outside in and offset with round joins, the paths of sortable infill collections are chained one by one, and narrow internal solid bands are their own collections, clipped at the end and ordered nearest end first. 2026-10-01: the default wall generator changed to aegis (our implementation of preFlight's Athena method; athena stays an alias). The reference plate pins classic walls, so no hash changed. FNV-1a 64 of the reference plate outputs (packages/core/bench/configs/reference-0.20.json). Update with the change that alters output and say why. 2026-09-30: walls that hang over the layer below are written as overhang wall pieces (the reference X leans 40 degrees and has rounded plinth edges); toolpaths and extrusion are unchanged. Same day: layers under slow_down_layer_time are slowed (min layer time), the part cooling fan is written per layer, so speeds and the time estimate changed. 2026-09-30, parity with OrcaSlicer: bead spacing is the flow spacing (w - h(1 - pi/4)), sparse infill lines are joined along the wall, only the visible top layer is Top surface (the shell under it is internal solid), the first solid layer over sparse infill is an internal bridge, and only beads hanging completely free are overhang walls. 2026-09-30, firmware output: every layer chunk ends with a ;@L marker (time and extrusion) and the file with a ;@F marker, which finalize turns into M73 progress and the statistics footer; a resume start lifts before homing X and Y. 2026-09-30, path parity with OrcaSlicer: solid surfaces and ironing are linked monotonic zigzags with turns along the wall (top, bottom and internal solid patterns read as Orca's defaults), sparse rectilinear infill is one sweep joined along the walls, curves are drawn in the layer's fill-angle frame, arc fitting follows ArcFitter, spiral lift no longer writes a stray line, and the per-layer T0 of a single tool is gone. Later the same day: infill lines that cannot join another line follow the wall as a hook (Orca connect_infill: sparse_infill_anchor, sparse_infill_anchor_max), sparse pockets under minimum_sparse_infill_area print as internal solid infill. Sparse rectilinear and aligned infill follow the partner rule of Orca's connect_segment_intersections_by_contours (turns on the inner contour, ends on the outer one, no detour cap: spikes at tooth roots came from the segment-count distance). 2026-09-30, surface classification as Orca does it: top and bottom surfaces are the layer outline less its neighbor's, the solid shells come from discover_vertical_shells (ensure_all, now the default when the setting is absent) or discover_horizontal_shells, surfaces grow into the shell and sparse areas beside them as in process_external_surfaces, narrow internal solid bands are filled with variable-width beads (split_solid_surface, FillConcentricInternal), and the first solid layer over sparse infill is an internal bridge anchored to the infill lines below (bridge_over_infill), with a solid ring kept under its edges at the walls. External bridges as Orca grows them (expand_bridges_detect_orientations: a bridge grows into the shell, sparse and top areas beside it, its direction is the one crossing the fewest floating edges). Brim as Orca writes it (Brim.cpp): an even number of line spacings wide (12 loops for 5 mm at 0.42), each one spacing from the last with round corners, so the first layer extrudes as much as Orca's. Narrow internal solid fill runs on the part of the band that lies inside the inner contour less the overlap (no_overlap_expolygons). Surface lines that are not linked (monotonicline top surfaces) now run out to the surface pulled in 0.05 of a spacing, as the linked ones always did, instead of stopping at the half-spacing inner contour. Where the inner contour is pinched, a line runs out only halfway to the next span of its line. 2026-09-30, seam placement as Orca SeamPlacer: seams are planned for the whole object (candidate points scored by wall angle, surface visibility from a raycast, overhang and hidden position, aligned into strings fitted by a cubic B-spline), so seam positions changed. 2026-09-30, seam gap: every closed loop ends seam_gap (10 percent of the nozzle by default) short of its start as Orca clips it (brim and skirt loops included), and scarf seams exist; the wipe checks read a loop as closed when it ends within a millimeter of its start. 2026-10-01, seam ties: candidates of a wall start at the lowest, leftmost vertex of the counterclockwise ring (Orca takes the first of equal candidates in its Clipper ring order), so equal corners go to the first one of that ring. 2026-10-01, brim areas as Orca builds them: the outline before elephant foot compensation (unless brim_use_efc_outline), one area per filament cut into loops by the Orca inward offset sequence, pieces that touch nothing dropped. 2026-09-30, writer parity: Z moves (layer change and lifts) run at travel_speed_z, or the travel speed when that is 0 (Orca GCodeWriter::_travel_to_z), instead of a fixed 20 mm/s; the first layer travels at initial_layer_travel_speed. 2026-10-01, offsets: a shape shrunk past its narrowest width now vanishes (the union offset runs the overlapping joins back through the vertex as Clipper does, and the fast miter offset is refused when its points land closer to the contour than the offset); before, a small convex island shrunk too far came back turned inside out, so thin parts of the reference X lose inner pieces that should not exist. 2026-10-01, print order as Orca: the infill phase chains the fill collections and the gap beads nearest first from where the walls end and the paths inside a collection too unless its pattern keeps its own order (ShortestPath.cpp chain_extrusion_entities, GCode::extrude_infill), and an island's walls print as Orca's loop tree (innermost wall of each nested loop first), which cuts travel on the gear from 86 m to 24 m. This hash also carries changes by others that landed since the previous update. 2026-10-01, core-2: the slice gets Orca's gap closing (slice_closing_radius 0.049 mm, grow then shrink, contours simplified at 0.0025 mm), skirt and brim loops start at the point nearest the nozzle (the skirt's first loop at skirt_start_angle) instead of by the seam rule. 2026-10-01, feed rates: a path whose speed equals the previous path's no longer skips its G1 F when a travel, retraction, wipe or lift wrote another F in between (G0 and G1 share the feed rate, so such paths ran at the travel or retraction feed); the writer now tracks the last F written on any move, as Orca's cooling buffer does; the added G1 F lines move the G-code line numbers the SXPV extras carry. This hash also carries output changes by others that landed since the previous update. 2026-10-01, overhangs and bridges (in the same hash as the feed rate fix): walls, overhang walls and bridges take Orca's point by point overhang speed (quality.rs, ExtrusionQualityEstimator) in place of step tiers, overhang walls print at the bridge speed, and the bridge defaults are Orca's: thick_bridges off (flat beads), bridge_line_width 100 percent of the nozzle, internal_bridge_speed 150 percent of bridge_speed. 2026-10-01, cooling as Orca's CoolingBuffer: a layer under slow_down_layer_time caps its fastest paths first at one common speed (no longer slows every path in proportion), with layer times in the cooling buffer's model (no acceleration, from the first extrusion), and the part fan reads that time; a slope lift ramps at the travel speed. 2026-10-01, gap fill as Orca's ExPolygon::medial_axis: free ends of the axis run on to the outline, lines with a free end shorter than twice the widest go, the lines left meeting end to end join again, and a bead cut where its width changes stays one stroke in the print order (ExtrusionMultiPath), so the gear's gap fill is one 1.8 mm bead per tooth (Orca 1.75) where it was two pieces of 1.1 and 0.4 mm. 2026-10-01, defaults from the settings schema: a key the reference config leaves out now takes the schema's process default (packages/settings/defaults.json, what the app starts from) in place of the engine's own, for example 0.45 mm lines where the profile has none, 0.4 mm support lines, three top interface layers and the schema's accelerations, so support filament on the support cases drops about 5 to 7 percent (narrower support lines) as intended. Keys the reference config sets are unchanged. 2026-10-01, two fixes found on the MK4S x-reference: an inward offset of a ring thinner than twice the offset no longer leaves its grown hole behind as a stray shape (the fast offset now checks its points against every contour of the shape, not only its own), which put a one-line band of solid infill around the plinth on ten layers; and on the elephant foot layers the layers beside them see the outline before the foot compensation, as Orca's lslices are, so the second layer no longer bridges the compensated strip (bridge 95 against Orca's 95 mm on that layer, was 815).
